newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico '97 textile exports to grow 20 pct - industry.
newsitem.headline: Mexico '97 textile exports to grow 20 pct - industry.

text.p: Mexico's textile industry could boost exports by 20 percent in 1997 compared with 1996 levels, an industry leader told Reuters on Friday.
"We increased exports by 20 percent this year (1996), we could do the same in 1997," said Jose Saltiel, president of the National Textile Industry Chamber.
Saltiel said final export figures for 1996 were not available, but said exports for the first eight months of the year were $806 million, some 20 percent above the same period of 1995.
Saltiel said growth in exports would henceforth be more moderate and predictable than the 150 percent increase in exports the industry saw in 1995.
This increase in exports means Mexico is now the main supplier of textiles to the United States, he said.
Saltiel said Mexico was still a major importer of textiles, however. "Total imports for the year to August in 1996 were $550 million," he said.
The boom in exports was in contrast to the decline in domestic sales in recent years in the wake of the 1995 economic crisis, and had benefitted a small number of producers.
"All that we are exporting, we would be selling on the domestic market, which is our natural market, if we had the purchasing power," Saltiel said.
"Strong exporters only account for eight percent of the firms in the industry, 95-percent of which are small businesses," he added.
